pairs.fullEnglish: The life of שרה was a hundred and twenty-seven years: the years of the life of שרה.
שרה died in קרית ארבע, which is חברון, in the land of כנען; אברהם came to mourn שרה and to weep for her.
אברהם rose from before his dead and spoke with the children of חת, saying:
I am a sojourner and a resident among you. Give me a burial possession among you, so that I may bury my dead from before me.
The children of חת answered אברהם, saying to him:
Accept from us, lord of ours: great before יְיָ are you among us. In the choicest of our graves bury your dead. None of us will withhold his grave from you, preventing you from burying your dead.
אברהם rose and bowed to the people of the land, to the children of חת.
He spoke with them, saying: If there is willingness in your souls for me to bury my dead from before me, accept from me, and ask עפרון son of צוחר on my behalf:
Let him give me the double cave that belongs to him, which is at the edge of his field. For the full price in silver let him give it to me among you as a burial possession.
עפרון was sitting among the children of חת. עפרון of חת answered אברהם before the children of חת, before all who entered the gate of his city, saying:
No, my lord, accept from me: I have given you the field, and the cave in it I have given to you. In the sight of the children of my people I have given it to you. Bury your dead.
אברהם bowed before the people of the land.

He spoke with עפרון before the people of the land, saying: But if you are doing me a kindness, accept from me: I will give silver, the price of the field. Take it from me, and I will bury my dead there.
עפרון answered אברהם, saying to him:
My lord, accept from me: land worth four hundred sela-weights of silver—between me and you, what is that? Bury your dead.

אברהם accepted from עפרון, and אברהם weighed out for עפרון the silver that he had stated before the children of חת: four hundred sela-weights of silver, accepted in trade (variant accepted in commerce), in every province.
The field of עפרון in כפלתא, which faces ממרא—the field, the cave in it, and all the trees in the field, throughout its entire boundary all around—was established
as the purchase of אברהם, in the sight of the children of חת, before all who entered the gate of his city.
After this, אברהם buried שרה his wife in the cave of the field of כפלתא, facing ממרא, which is חברון, in the land of כנען.
The field and the cave in it were established as a burial possession for אברהם from the children of חת.
אברהם was old, advanced in days, and ייָ had blessed אברהם in everything.
אברהם said to his servant, the elder of his household, who had authority over all that was his: Place your hand now under my thigh.
I will put you under oath by the Word of יְיָ, God of heaven and God of earth, that you will not take a wife for my son from the daughters of the Canaanites among whom I dwell.
His servant said to him: Perhaps the woman will not be willing to come after me to this land. Shall I indeed bring your son back to the land from which you went out?
אברהם said to him: Take care lest you bring my son back there.

יְיָ, God of heaven, who led me from my father's house and from the land of my birth, who spoke to me and who swore to me, saying, To your son I will give this land—He will send His angel before you, and you shall take a wife for my son from there.
If the woman is not willing to come after you, you shall be free of this oath of mine. Only do not bring my son back there.
The servant placed his hand under the thigh of אברהם his master and swore to him concerning this matter.
The servant took ten camels from his master's camels and went, with all the choicest things of his master in his hand. He arose and went to ארם which is on פרת, to the city of נחור.
He settled the camels outside the city by the well of water, at evening time, at the time when the women who draw water go out.
He said: יְיָ, God of my master אברהם, arrange an encounter before me now, this day, and show kindness to my master אברהם.
Here I stand by the spring of water, and the daughters of the people of the city are coming out to draw water.

Let it be that the young woman to whom I say, Lower your pitcher now so that I may drink, and who says, Drink, and I will also water your camels—her You have appointed for Your servant, for יצחק. Through her I shall know that You have shown kindness to my master.
Before he had finished speaking, behold, רבקה came out, who had been born to בתואל, son of מלכה, the wife of נחור, אברהם's brother; her pitcher was on her shoulder.

The young woman was exceedingly beautiful in appearance (<small>variant</small> beautiful to look upon), a virgin, and no man had known her. She went down to the spring, filled her pitcher and came up.
The servant ran to meet her and said: Let me drink (<small>other reading</small> let me taste), now, a little water from your pitcher.
She said: Drink, my lord. She hurried, lowered her pitcher onto her hand and gave him to drink.
When she had finished giving him to drink, she said: For your camels also I will draw, until they have had enough to drink.
She hurried and emptied her pitcher into the watering trough, ran again to the well to draw, and drew for all his camels.
The man lingered over her, watching silently, to know whether יְיָ had made his journey successful or not.
He said: Whose daughter are you? Tell me now: is there in your father's house a suitable place for us to spend the night?
She said to him: I am the daughter of בתואל, the son of מלכא, whom she bore to נחור.
She said to him: We have both straw and plenty of fodder, and also a suitable place to spend the night.
The man bent down and bowed before יְיָ.

He said: Blessed is יְיָ, God of my master אברהם, who has not withheld His kindness and His faithfulness from my master. As for me, יְיָ has led me on a right path to the house of my master's brothers.
The young woman ran and told her mother's household these things.
רבקה had a brother whose name was לבן. לבן ran outside to the man, to the spring.

When he saw the nose-ring and the bracelets on his sister's hands, and when he heard the words of רבקה his sister, saying, Thus the man spoke with me, he came to the man; behold, he was standing beside the camels at the spring.
He said: Come in, blessed of יְיָ. Why are you standing outside, when I have cleared the house and a suitable place for the camels?
They set food before him to eat, but he said: I will not eat until I have spoken my words. He said: Speak.
He said: I am the servant of אברהם.
ייָ has blessed my master exceedingly, and he has become great. He has given him sheep and cattle, silver and gold, male servants and female servants, camels and donkeys.
שרה, my master's wife, bore a son to my master after she had grown old, and he gave him all that was his.
My master put me under oath, saying: You shall not take a wife for my son from the daughters of the Canaanites in whose land I dwell.
Rather, you shall go to my father's house and to my family, and take a wife for my son.
I said to my master: Perhaps the woman will not come after me.
He said to me: יְיָ, before whom I have served, will send His angel with you and make your journey successful. You shall take a wife for my son from my family and from my father's house.
Then you shall be free (<small>variant</small> free) of my oath, when you go to my family; and if they do not give her to you, you shall be free of my oath.
I came (variant I came) this day to the spring and said: יְיָ, God of my master אברהם, if now it is Your will to make successful my journey on which I am going:
Here I stand by the spring of water. Let it be that the young woman who comes out to draw, to whom I say, Give me now a little water to drink from your pitcher,
and who says to me, Both you drink, and for your camels also I will draw—she is the woman whom יְיָ has appointed for my master's son.
Before I had finished speaking in my heart, behold, רבקה came out, her pitcher on her shoulder. She went down to the spring and drew, and I said to her: Give me to drink now.
She hurried and lowered her pitcher from herself and said: Drink, and I will also water your camels. I drank, and she also watered the camels.
I asked her and said: Whose daughter are you? She said: The daughter of בתואל, the son of נחור, whom מלכה bore to him. I put the nose-ring on her nose and the bracelets on her hands.
I bent down and bowed before יְיָ, and blessed יְיָ, God of my master אברהם, who led me on a path of truth to take the daughter of my master's brother for his son.
Now, if you are showing kindness and faithfulness to my master, tell me; and if not, tell me, so that I may turn to the right or to the left.
לבן and בתואל answered and said: The matter has gone forth from before יְיָ. We cannot speak with you either bad or good.
Here is רבקה before you. Take her and go, and let her be a wife to your master's son, as יְיָ has spoken.
When אברהם's servant heard their words, he bowed to the ground before יְיָ.
The servant brought out articles of silver and articles of gold and garments and gave them to רבקה; and he gave choice gifts to her brother and her mother.
He and the men who were with him ate and drank, and spent the night. They arose in the morning, and he said: Send me away to my master.
Her brother and her mother said: Let the young woman remain with us a full year, or ten months; afterward she shall go.
He said to them: Do not delay me, since ייָ has made my journey successful. Send me away, and I shall go to my master.
They said: Let us call the young woman and hear what she says.
They called רבקה and said to her: Will you go with this man? She said: I will go.
They sent away רבקה their sister, her nurse, אברהם's servant and his men.
They blessed רבקה and said to her: Our sister, may you become thousands and myriads, and may your children inherit the cities of those who hate them.
רבקה and her young women arose, rode on the camels and went after the man. The servant took רבקה and went.
יצחק went out to pray in the field toward evening. He raised his eyes and saw, and behold, camels were coming.
רבקה raised her eyes and saw יצחק, and lowered herself from upon the camel.
She said to the servant: Who is that man walking in the field to meet us? The servant said: He is my master. She took the veil and covered herself.
The servant recounted to יצחק all the things he had done.

יצחק brought her into the tent, and saw that, behold, her deeds were right, like the deeds of שרה his mother. He took רבקה, and she became his wife, and he loved her. יצחק was comforted after his mother had died.
אברהם again took a wife, and her name was קטורה.
She bore him זמרן, יקשן, מדן, מדין, ישבק and שוח.
The children of מדין were עיפה, עפר, חנוך, אבידע and אלדעה. All these were the children of קטורה.
אברהם gave all that was his to יצחק.
To the sons of the concubines who belonged to אברהם, אברהם gave gifts, and sent them away from יצחק his son, while he was still living, eastward, to the eastern land.
These were the days of the years of אברהם's life which he lived: a hundred and seventy-five years.
אברהם expired and died in a good old age, old and full of days, and was gathered to his people.
יצחק and ישמעאל his sons buried him in the double cave, in the field of עפרון son of צחר the Hittite, which faces ממרא.
The field was the one that אברהם bought from the children of חת. There אברהם and שרה his wife were buried.
After אברהם died, יְיָ blessed יצחק his son. יצחק dwelt by the well at which the angel of the Ever-Living One had appeared.
These are the generations of ישמעאל son of אברהם, whom הגר the Egyptian, שרה's maidservant, bore to אברהם.
These are the names of the sons of ישמעאל, by their names according to their generations: the firstborn of ישמעאל, נביות; then קדר, אדבאל and מבשם;
and משמע, דומה and משא;
חדד and תימא, יטור, נפיש and קדמה.
These are the sons of ישמעאל, and these are their names by their unwalled settlements and their fortified towns: twelve chiefs according to their peoples.
These were the years of ישמעאל's life: a hundred and thirty-seven years. He expired and died and was gathered to his people.
They dwelt from חוילה as far as חגרא, which faces מצרים as one comes to אתור. He dwelt opposite all his brothers.
Rather, you shall go to my land and to my native place, and take a wife for my son, for יצחק.
When they had had enough—the camels—to drink, the man took a gold nose-ring, a תִּקְלָא in weight, and two bracelets for her hands, ten sela-weights of gold being their weight.

qualifications.he: שם המשקל תִּקְלָא נשמר כלשונו. היחס המדויק שלו לסלע לא הוכרע כאן; אין לקרוא לתוך הטיוטה המרה ליחידת משקל אחרת.
qualifications.en: The weight-unit name תִּקְלָא is retained as supplied. Its exact relation to the sela has not been resolved here; this draft does not assert a conversion to another weight unit.

pairs.fullEnglish: The man entered the house. The camels were unbound, and straw and fodder were given to the camels, along with water to wash his feet and the feet of the men who were with him.

qualifications.he: לאחר כניסת האיש לבית, הפועלים וּשְׁרָא וִיהַב באים בלשון נסתר יחיד בלי שם מפורש של הפועל. האנגלית משתמשת כאן בלשון סבילה כדי לא להכריע אם האורח או המארח התיר את הגמלים ונתן את המספוא והמים. זהות הפועל נשארת בלתי מוכרעת; לשון המקור לא שונתה.
qualifications.en: After the man's entrance into the house, וּשְׁרָא and וִיהַב are third-person masculine singular verbs without an explicitly named actor. The English uses passive wording here so as not to decide whether the guest or the host unbound the camels and supplied the fodder and water. The actor's identity remains unresolved; the source wording is unchanged.

pairs.fullEnglish: King David had grown old and advanced in days. They covered him with garments, but he did not become warm.
His servants said to him, ‘Let them seek a young virgin for my lord the king. Let her serve before the king and be an attendant close to him; let her lie beside you and warm my lord the king.’
They sought a beautiful young woman throughout the territory of the land of Israel. They found Avishag, who was from שׁוּנֵם, and brought her to the king.
The young woman was exceedingly beautiful. She became an attendant close to the king and served him, but the king did not have intimate relations with her.
Adonijah son of חַגִית exalted himself, saying, ‘I shall reign.’ He provided himself with chariots and horsemen, and fifty men running before him.
They do not sleep until they do evil, and their sleep departs until they cause a stumbling.
For their food is the food of the wicked, and they drink the wine of robbers.
The path of the righteous is like a light that shines, its brightness continuing to grow until the day is fully established.
The path of the wicked is dark, and they do not know what makes them stumble.
My son, listen to my words, and incline your ear to my sayings.
He held consultations with יוֹאָב son of צְרוּיָה and with אֶבְיָתָר the priest, and they lent their support to Adonijah.
But צָדוֹק the priest, בְּנָיָהוּ son of יְהוֹיָדָע, Nathan the prophet, שִׁמְעִי, רֵעִי, and David’s mighty men were not party to Adonijah’s counsel.
But Nathan the prophet, בְּנָיָהוּ, the mighty men, and his brother Solomon he did not invite.
Let them not depart from your eyes; keep them within your heart.
For they are life to whoever finds them, and healing to all his flesh.
With every precaution guard your heart, for from it comes the outflow of life.
Remove crookedness of mouth from yourself, and keep perversity of lips far from yourself.
Nathan said to Bathsheba, Solomon’s mother, ‘Have you not heard that Adonijah son of חַגִית has become king, while our lord David does not know?’

‘Go and enter the presence of King David, and say to him: “Did you not, my lord the king, swear to your maidservant, saying, ‘Your son Solomon shall reign after me, and he shall sit upon my royal throne’? Why, then, has Adonijah become king?”’
‘And look: while you are still speaking there before the king, I shall enter after you and confirm your words.’
Bathsheba entered the king’s presence, into the bedchamber. The king was very old, and Avishag, who was from שׁוּנֵם, was serving before the king.
Remove your feet from evil paths, and all your ways will be set right.
Do not turn aside to the right or to the left; remove your feet from evil.
My son, listen to my wisdom; incline your ear to my understanding.
So that you may be watchful in your thinking, and your lips may preserve knowledge.
Bathsheba knelt and bowed down to the king. The king said, ‘What is your concern?’
She said to him, ‘My lord, you swore by the Word of ייָ, your God, to your maidservant: “Your son Solomon shall reign after me, and he shall sit upon my royal throne.”’
‘And now, look: Adonijah has become king, and you, my lord the king, did not know.’

‘He has slaughtered cattle, fattened animals, and sheep in abundance, and has invited all the king’s sons, אֶבְיָתָר the priest, and יוֹאָב the commander of the army; but Solomon your servant he did not invite.’
‘And now, my lord the king, the eyes of all Israel look expectantly to you to tell them who will sit upon the royal throne of my lord the king after him.’
‘And it will be, when my lord the king lies down with his fathers, that I and my son Solomon will be driven out.’
Her feet descend to death; her steps lead to the realm of the dead.
She does not tread the path of life; her tracks wander, and she does not know.
And now, children, listen to me, and do not turn aside from the sayings of my mouth.
Keep your way far from her, and do not approach the door of her house.
And look: while she was still speaking with the king, Nathan the prophet arrived.
They informed the king, saying, ‘Here is Nathan the prophet.’ He came before the king and bowed down to the king with his face to the ground.
Nathan said, ‘My lord the king, did you say, “Adonijah shall reign after me, and he shall sit upon my royal throne”?’

‘For he has gone down today and slaughtered cattle, fattened animals, and sheep in abundance, and has invited all the king’s sons, the army commanders, and אֶבְיָתָר the priest. Look: they are eating and drinking before him, and they have said, “May King Adonijah prosper!”’
‘But me, your servant, and צָדוֹק the priest, בְּנָיָהוּ son of יְהוֹיָדָע, and Solomon your servant, he did not invite.’
Lest you give your strength to others and your years to foreigners.
Lest foreigners be sated with your resources, and your toil enter the house of others.
And you groan at your end, until your flesh and your body are consumed.
And you say, ‘How I hated discipline, and my heart disregarded reproof!’
‘I did not listen to the voice of my masters, and I did not incline my ears to my teachers.’
His father had never in his days put him to shame by saying, ‘Why are you acting like this?’ He too was very handsome in appearance, and she bore him after Absalom.

qualifications.he: הפועל ילידת הוא בנקבה, אך נושאו אינו נקוב בפסוק זה. הניסוח 'היא ילדה אותו אחרי אבשלום' משמר את הנושא המשתמע בלי לנקוב בשמו. אין במשפט זה קביעה שאדוניה ואבשלום נולדו לאותה אם.
qualifications.en: The verb 'bore' has a feminine subject, but that subject is not named in this verse. 'She bore him after Absalom' preserves the implied subject without naming her. This sentence does not establish that Adonijah and Absalom had the same mother.

pairs.fullEnglish: Adonijah slaughtered sheep, cattle, and fattened animals at the lookout stone, which is beside the fuller's spring. He invited all his brothers, the king’s sons, and all the men of Judah who were servants of the king.

qualifications.he: ׳אבן התצפית׳ נשען על הסברו המפורש של רש״י ללשון יונתן: ׳וְיוֹנָתָן תִּרְגֵּם: אֶבֶן סְכוּתָא, שֶׁעוֹמְדִין עָלֶיהָ וְצוֹפִין לְמֵרָחוֹק׳. גם עֵין קַצְרָא מוסבר אצלו במפורש כלשון יונתן המציינת את הכובס. דִין נקרא כאן כמילת רמיזה החוזרת אל המקום המתואר: ׳זה לצד מעיין הכובס׳; משפט הזיקה באנגלית מוסר את הקשר המקומי הזה. רש״י אינו מפרש כאן את דִין: קריאה זו נשענת על הצירוף הארמי, בלי לשנות את דִין לדִי ובלי להוסיף שם מקום. פירושו הנפרד של רש״י על הבחורים המזיזים את האבן אינו נכלל בתרגום, וגם משמעות של סוכה או מחסה אינה נוספת לו.
qualifications.en: 'Lookout stone' rests on Rashi's explicit explanation of Jonathan's wording: 'וְיוֹנָתָן תִּרְגֵּם: אֶבֶן סְכוּתָא, שֶׁעוֹמְדִין עָלֶיהָ וְצוֹפִין לְמֵרָחוֹק'—people stand on it and watch into the distance. He also expressly identifies Jonathan's עֵין קַצְרָא with the fuller. דִין is read here as a deictic resuming the described location, 'this [one/site] is beside the fuller's spring'; the English relative clause conveys that location relation. Rashi does not explain דִין here: this reading rests on the Aramaic construction, without changing דִין to דִי or adding a place-name. Rashi's separate explanation about young men moving the stone is not included in the translation, nor is a booth or shelter sense added.
qualifications.anchor: אֶבֶן סְכוּתָא דִין בִּסְטַר עֵין קַצְרָא

pairs.fullEnglish: But her end is bitter like an arrow, sharper than a two-edged sword.

qualifications.he: גִירָא נמסרת בהוראתה הרגילה 'חץ', בצירוף לדימוי הנשק הבא, חרב בעלת שני פיות. המרירות מתארת אחרית קשה ומכאיבה; הדימוי אינו מחייב שלחץ יש טעם מר. אין כאן זיהוי של צמח, רעל או חץ משוח ברעל, ואין החלפה ב'לענה' מן הפסוק העברי.
qualifications.en: גִירָא is rendered in its ordinary sense 'arrow,' alongside the following weapon image of a two-edged sword. Bitterness describes a grievous, painful end; the image does not require an arrow to have a bitter taste. No plant, poison or poison-coated arrow is identified, and 'wormwood' from the Hebrew verse is not substituted.

pairs.fullEnglish: יקשן fathered שבא and דדן. The children of דדן became camps, settlements and island communities.

qualifications.he: שלושת השמות באים אחרי הֲווֹ בלמ״ד התוצאה: בני דדן נעשו קבוצות של מחנות, יישובים וקהילות איים. נַגְוָן מציין כאן את קבוצות האיים, אך אינו מזהה איים מסוימים או עם מאוחר. אין אלה שלושה בנים נוספים. רש״י מבאר במפורש את לְמַשִּׁירְיָן כלשון מחנה, אך אומר שאין בידו ליישב את תרגום אונקלוס עם לשון שמות האומות שבמקרא; הקושי הזה בהתאמה לשמות נשאר בעינו.
qualifications.en: The three nouns follow הֲווֹ with resultative לְ: the children of דדן became groups of camps, settlements and island communities. נַגְוָן denotes the island groups here, without identifying particular islands or a later people. These are not three additional sons. Rashi expressly explains לְמַשִּׁירְיָן as camp language, but says he cannot reconcile Onkelos's rendering with the Biblical wording of the national names; that difficulty in matching the names remains.

pairs.fullEnglish: Let your eyes shine with uprightness, and let your eyelashes be directed straight before you.

qualifications.he: נְאוֹרָן משמרת כאן את דימוי האור שבעיניים: ׳יאירו ביושר׳, ולא רק פועל כללי של הסתכלות. תִמָרָיִךְ הן ריסי העיניים; בצלע המקבילה הם מופנים ישר לפנים. היושר הוא גם לשון כיוון וגם דימוי לדרך ישרה; אין בתיאור קביעה רפואית על העיניים.
qualifications.en: נְאוֹרָן retains the image of light in the eyes: 'shine with uprightness,' rather than merely a general verb of looking. תִמָרָיִךְ denotes the eyelashes, directed straight ahead in the parallel clause. Straightness carries both directional language and the image of an upright course; this is not a medical statement about the eyes.
qualifications.anchor: עַיְנָךְ בִּתְרִיצוּתָא נְאוֹרָן וְתִמָרָיִךְ נִתְרְצוּן לְקוּבְלָךְ

pairs.fullEnglish: For the foreign woman's lips drip honey from the comb, and her palate is smoother than oil.

qualifications.he: כַבְרִיתָא היא כאן חלת דבש. בצירוף שבו השפתיים נוטפות, שם החלה מציין בהשאלה את הדבש הנוטף ממנה; זו משמעות הניסוח האנגלי ״דבש מן החלה״, ולא תיאור של שיטת הפקת דבש. הדל״ת שלאחר מְטוּל פותחת את משפט ההסבר ואינה מילת דימוי שמשמעה ״כמו״. אין כאן קביעה שהשפתיים נוטפות חתיכות חלה, זיהוי של דרגת דבש מודרנית או החלפת המילה הארמית בנֹפֶת שבמקרא. במילון נרשמו גם כתיבים וקריאות של מהדורות אחרות לשם כַבְרִיתָא. השפתיים הן נושא הפועל ברבים, ואילו חִכָּהּ הוא החך היחיד המושווה לשמן בצלע השנייה.
qualifications.en: כַבְרִיתָא here means honeycomb. In the construction in which the lips drip, the comb stands metonymically for its dripping honey; this is the force of the English 'honey from the comb,' not a description of a honey-extraction method. The דְ after מְטוּל introduces the explanatory clause; it is not a comparison marker meaning 'like.' The wording does not assert that the lips drip pieces of comb, identify a modern grade of honey, or replace the Aramaic noun with the biblical נֹפֶת. The dictionary also records variant spellings and readings of this noun in other editions. The plural lips are the subject of the dripping predicate, whereas חִכָּהּ is the separate singular palate compared with oil in the second clause.

dayTitle.en: The Death of שרה and the Request for a Burial Possession

explanation.he: לאחר מות שרה בחברון, אברהם קם מעל פני מתו ומבקש מבני חת אחוזת קבר. הם מכנים אותו רב לפני יי ומציעים לו לקבור במבחר קבריהם, בלי שאיש ימנע ממנו את קברו.
explanation.en: After שרה dies in חברון, אברהם rises from before his dead and asks the children of חת for a burial possession. They describe him as great before יְיָ and offer their choicest graves, with none of them withholding his grave.

dayTitle.en: The Request for the Cave in the Field of עפרון

explanation.he: אברהם משתחווה לבני חת ומבקש שיפנו בשבילו לעפרון בן צוחר. הוא מבקש את המערה הכפולה שבקצה השדה בכסף מלא, ותשובת עפרון ניתנת בפני באי שער עירו.
explanation.en: אברהם bows to the children of חת and asks them to approach עפרון son of צוחר on his behalf. He requests the double cave at the edge of the field for its full price, and עפרון answers publicly before those entering his city's gate.

dayTitle.en: The Offer of the Field and אברהם's Insistence on Payment

explanation.he: עפרון מציע את השדה ואת המערה שבו לעיני בני עמו. אברהם מבקש לשלם את מחיר השדה, ועפרון מציין את שוויו בארבע מאות סלעי כסף.
explanation.en: עפרון offers the field and its cave in the sight of his people. אברהם asks to pay the field's price, and עפרון states its value as four hundred sela-weights of silver.

dayTitle.en: Payment of the Silver and the Burial of שרה

explanation.he: אברהם שוקל לעפרון את הכסף שנקב בו בפני בני חת, והשדה עם המערה וכל עציו נקנה לו בפומבי. לאחר הקבורה הכתוב חוזר ומציין את אחוזת הקבר, ואחר כך מתאר את זקנת אברהם ואת הברכה שניתנה לו בכל.
explanation.en: אברהם weighs out the silver named by עפרון before the children of חת, and the field, cave and all its trees become his purchase publicly. After the burial, the account again states the establishment of the burial possession, then describes אברהם's old age and the blessing granted him in everything.

dayTitle.en: The Oath to Take a Wife for יצחק

explanation.he: אברהם מטיל על עבדו הזקן שבועה במימרא דיי שלא לקחת לבנו אשה מבנות הכנענים. הוא שולח אותו לארצו ולמקום מוצאו, אך מזהיר שלא להשיב לשם את בנו גם לנוכח האפשרות שהאשה לא תרצה לבוא.
explanation.en: אברהם places his elder servant under oath by the Word of יְיָ not to take a Canaanite wife for his son. He sends him to his own land and native place, but warns him not to bring his son back there when the servant raises the possibility that the woman may refuse to come.

dayTitle.en: The Prayer at the Spring and the Meeting with רבקה

explanation.he: אברהם אומר שיי ישלח את מלאכו לפני העבד, ופוטר את העבד מן השבועה אם האשה לא תרצה לבוא. על יד העין העבד מבקש סימן של חסד, ורבקה משקה אותו ואת גמליו ומספרת את ייחוסה. הוא משתחווה לפני יי ומודה על ההדרכה, ולאחר מכן לבן מזמין אותו לבית.
explanation.en: אברהם assures his servant that an angel will go before him, but releases him from the oath if the woman is unwilling to come. At the spring the servant asks for a sign of kindness, and רבקה waters him and his camels and identifies her family. He bows before יְיָ and gives thanks for the guidance, after which לבן invites him into the house.

dayTitle.he: שליחות העבד, נישואי רבקה ותולדות בית אברהם
dayTitle.en: The Servant's Mission, רבקה's Marriage and the Generations of אברהם's House

explanation.he: העבד מספר את שבועתו ואת תפילתו, ומשפחת רבקה מכירה בכך שהדבר יצא מלפני יי; רבקה עצמה אומרת שתלך. יצחק יוצא להתפלל, מקבל את רבקה, רואה שמעשיה מתוקנים כמעשי שרה אמו ונושא אותה. בהמשך נמנים בני קטורה, מתנות אברהם לבני הפילגשים, מותו וקבורתו, ולאחר מכן בני ישמעאל ומקומות מושבם.
explanation.en: The servant recounts his oath and prayer, and רבקה's family acknowledges that the matter has come from before יְיָ; רבקה herself says she will go. יצחק goes out to pray, receives רבקה, sees that her deeds are right like those of שרה his mother, and marries her. The reading then records קטורה's children, אברהם's gifts to the concubines' sons, his death and burial, and afterward ישמעאל's children and their places of settlement.

dayTitle.en: David’s Old Age and Adonijah’s Self-Exaltation

explanation.he: התרגום מתאר את זקנת דוד ואת הבאת אבישג משונם כדי לשרתו ולחממו, ומדגיש שהמלך לא ידעה. בהמשך אדוניה מכריז שימלוך ומעמיד לעצמו מרכבות, פרשים ורצים, ואביו אינו מוכיח אותו על מעשיו.
explanation.en: The Targum describes David’s old age and the arrival of Avishag from שׁוּנֵם to serve and warm him, expressly stating that the king did not have intimate relations with her. Adonijah then declares that he will reign and provides himself with chariots, horsemen, and runners, while his father does not rebuke his conduct.

dayTitle.he: להתרחק מדרכי הרשעים ולשמוע לדברי חכמה
dayTitle.en: Leaving the Wicked Path and Listening to Wisdom

explanation.he: התרגום מזהיר שלא ללכת עם הרשעים ומתאר את דבקותם ברעה ובגזל. מול דרכם החשוכה עומדת דרך הצדיקים, שאורה הולך ומתחזק, והקריאה מסתיימת בבקשה מן הבן להקשיב לדברי המורה.
explanation.en: The Targum warns against going with the wicked and describes their attachment to evil and robbery. Their dark path is contrasted with the steadily brightening path of the righteous, and the reading ends by asking the son to listen to his teacher’s words.

dayTitle.en: Adonijah’s Supporters and the Guests at His Feast

explanation.he: התרגום מונה את המסייעים לאדוניה ואת אנשי דוד שלא היו בעצתו. אדוניה שוחט בעלי חיים ומזמין את אחיו ואת עבדי המלך מיהודה, אך אינו מזמין את נתן, בניהו, הגיבורים ושלמה אחיו.
explanation.en: The Targum names those who supported Adonijah and those among David’s people who did not join his counsel. Adonijah slaughters animals and invites his brothers and the king’s servants from Judah, but leaves out Nathan, בְּנָיָהוּ, the mighty men, and his brother Solomon.

dayTitle.he: שמירת דברי החכמה בלב והרחקת דיבור עקום
dayTitle.en: Keeping Wisdom in the Heart and Crooked Speech Far Away

explanation.he: התרגום מצווה לשמור את דברי החכמה לעיני הלומד ובתוך לבו, ומתאר אותם כחיים למוצאיהם וכמרפא לכל בשרו. לאחר מכן הוא דורש שמירה על הלב והרחקת עקמימות הפה והשפתיים.
explanation.en: The Targum calls for keeping the words of wisdom before the learner’s eyes and within his heart, describing them as life to their finder and healing to all his flesh. It then calls for guarding the heart and removing crookedness from the mouth and lips.

dayTitle.he: עצת נתן לבת שבע להצלתה ולהצלת שלמה
dayTitle.en: Nathan’s Counsel to Save Bathsheba and Solomon

explanation.he: נתן מודיע לבת שבע שאדוניה מלך בלי ידיעת דוד, ומייעץ לה לפנות אל המלך כדי להציל את חייה ואת חיי שלמה בנה. הוא מבקש שתזכיר לדוד את שבועתו בעניין המלוכה, ומבטיח להיכנס אחריה ולאשר את דבריה.
explanation.en: Nathan tells Bathsheba that Adonijah has become king without David’s knowledge and advises her to approach the king to save her life and her son Solomon’s life. He asks her to remind David of his oath concerning the succession and promises to enter after her and confirm her words.

dayTitle.he: יושר העיניים, צעדים מתוקנים והקשבה לחכמה
dayTitle.en: Upright Eyes, Right Steps, and Attention to Wisdom

explanation.he: התרגום קורא ליושר העיניים ולהרחקת הרגליים משבילי רעה, בלי לסטות לימין או לשמאל. המעבר לפרק הבא מחדש את הקריאה לבן להקשיב לחכמה ולבינה, כדי להיזהר במחשבה ולשמור דעת בשפתיו.
explanation.en: The Targum calls for uprightness of the eyes and for removing one’s feet from evil paths, without turning right or left. The opening of the next chapter renews the appeal to the son to hear wisdom and understanding, so that he may be watchful in thought and preserve knowledge with his lips.

dayTitle.he: בת שבע מזכירה את השבועה ומבקשת הכרעה במלוכה
dayTitle.en: Bathsheba Recalls the Oath and Seeks a Decision on the Succession

explanation.he: בת שבע מזכירה לדוד שנשבע במימרא דייָ ששלמה ימלוך אחריו, ומספרת על המלכת אדוניה ועל הסעודה ששלמה לא הוזמן אליה. היא אומרת שעיני ישראל מצפות להכרעת המלך ומזהירה שלאחר מותו היא ובנה יהיו מגורשים.
explanation.en: Bathsheba reminds David that he swore by the Word of ייָ that Solomon would reign after him, and reports Adonijah’s kingship and the feast to which Solomon was not invited. She says that Israel looks to the king for a decision and warns that after his death she and her son will be driven out.

dayTitle.en: Enticing Speech and a Way That Leads to Death

explanation.he: התרגום מעמיד את דיבור האישה הנוכרייה, המתואר כחלק משמן, מול אחריתה המרה ודרכה היורדת למוות. הוא מתאר אותה כמי שאינה דורכת בדרך החיים, וקורא לבנים להקשיב למורה ולהרחיק את דרכם ממנה ומפתח ביתה.
explanation.en: The Targum contrasts the foreign woman’s speech, described as smoother than oil, with her bitter end and her descent toward death. It describes her as not walking the path of life and calls on the children to listen to the teacher and keep their way far from her and her doorway.

dayTitle.he: נתן מאשר את הדיווח ושואל על סמכות ההמלכה
dayTitle.en: Nathan Confirms the Report and Questions the Authority for the Kingship

explanation.he: נתן נכנס לפני דוד בעוד בת שבע מדברת עמו, ושואל אם המלך אמר שאדוניה ימלוך אחריו. הוא מתאר את הסעודה ואת הקריאה להצלחת אדוניה, ומונה את עבדי המלך שלא הוזמנו ובהם שלמה.
explanation.en: Nathan enters David’s presence while Bathsheba is still speaking with him and asks whether the king said that Adonijah would succeed him. He describes the feast and the wish for Adonijah’s success, then names the king’s servants who were not invited, including Solomon.

dayTitle.he: אובדן הכוח והחרטה על דחיית המוסר
dayTitle.en: Lost Strength and Regret for Rejecting Discipline

explanation.he: התרגום ממשיך את האזהרה מפני מסירת הכוח והשנים לאחרים, ומפני העברת פרי העמל לבית זרים. הוא מתאר את אנחת האדם בסופו ואת חרטתו על ששנא מוסר ולא הקשיב למוריו ולמלמדיו.
explanation.en: The Targum continues the warning against giving one’s strength and years to others and letting one’s toil pass into a stranger’s house. It describes the person’s groaning at his end and his regret for hating discipline and refusing to listen to his masters and teachers.
